To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

conditional mean embeddings can be interpreted as vector-valued regressions, and that the sparse conditional mean embedding can be interpreted as a vector-valued regression with sparsity inducing penalty.

1) conditional mean embeddings (CMEs) are equivalent to vector-valued regressions, 2) CMEs are minimax rate optimal, 3) we can obtain sparse CMEs by applying sparsity inducing vector-valued regression techniques, and 4) the sparsity induced by our method is better than the sparsity induced via incomplete Cholesky decompositions.

conditional mean embeddings can be interpreted as vector-valued regressions, and that this interpretation allows the application of results and algorithms for vector-valued learning to the conditional mean embedding problem.

the embedding is a natural and effective tool in the context of learning conditional distributions.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that the conditional mean embedding is a natural and intuitive regressor for learning conditional distributions.
we provide a new perspective to the problem of conditional mean embeddings as regressor, and show that the embeddings are indeed powerful tools to learn the conditional distribution.
we provide a new understanding of conditional mean embeddings, and a new sparse version of them.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the conditional mean embedding is a vector valued regressor, and as such it can be analysed, regularised and extended using tools from vector valued regression.
conditional mean embeddings can be viewed and used as a form of regularized vector-valued regression.
conditional distribution embeddings are a natural and powerful alternative to the standard regression framework for modelling conditional distributions.
